question: What is the formula for calculating the momentum of an object? (p = momentum, m = mass, a = acceleration, v = velocity)
solution:
The correct answer is __**p = mv**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Momentum** is a fundamental concept in physics, defined as the product of an object's **mass (m)** and its **velocity (v)**. The formula is expressed as **p = mv**.
 
• Here, **p** represents momentum, a vector quantity that has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Momentum is directly proportional to both the mass and velocity of the object. Thus, if the mass or velocity increases, the momentum also increases.
 
• The unit of momentum in the **International System of Units (SI)** is **kilogram meter per second (kg·m/s)**.
